the incidence of PH in the commercial airline population was 1.1 per 1 million passenger miles, that the majority of cases were mild, and that there was no association between PH and the presence of other medical conditions.

The risk of pulmonary embolism in air travelers with a prior history of venous thromboembolism is 1 in 2,000, and the risk of pulmonary embolic events in air travelers with no prior history of venothromboembolism, but with risk factors for pulmonary embolism, is 1 in. 5 million.

the incidence of pulmonary hypertension in commercial air travel is 0.1%, that the incidence of dyspnea and hypoxemia is 0.4 and 2.3%, respectively, that the risk factors for hypoxemia are female sex, age > 60, and obesity (BMI > 30 kg/m2), and that the risk factors of pulmonary hypertension are female sex, obesity (BMI >30 kg/m2) and a history of heart failure.
